chapter: Memphis boyhood and the Ohio territory years
title: Nineteen dollars with pianist Bobbie Brown and a bag of hot dogs
summary: Crawford takes a two-person gig with pianist Bobbie Brown in Cleveland and spends the pay on hot dogs for the hungry band.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Well, we got paid. In the meantime, while in Cleveland still a-starving -- this was in, 'round about 1931 or '32 -- Colored, nice looking woman by the name of Brown, Bobbie Brown, pianist, oh, you know, well, she needed a drummer one night. It was just the two of us, Bobbie Brown and Jimmy Crawford.

So I accepted the gig, naturally. I was hungry. And so she gave me $19.00 for the gig. That was more money than I ever had in my life. Me in turn took that -- took part of it or most of it and bought up a whole bag of hot dogs and threw some peanuts in there also, can't get away from those peanuts, and went back to the Majestic Hotel, woke everybody up in the band and said, hey, fellows, let's eat. Whole bag, a bag two feet tall or something like that.
And we sat and ate the hot dogs, baby, and that was my -- oh, that was like a (inaudible) featured meal. And we ate it. Then eventually we tripped on over to Buffalo, New York --
